title: A sticky situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum

words.zh: 棘手的局面、尴尬的处境
words.note: sticky 本义“黏的”，引申为“棘手的、难办的”：a sticky problem（棘手的问题）。
words.ctx: A sticky situation: why Singapore still won't sell you chewing gum

ex.en: Forgetting her name put me in a [[sticky situation]].
ex.zh: 忘了她的名字让我很尴尬。

ex.en: He talked his way out of a [[sticky situation]].
ex.zh: 他靠一张嘴摆脱了困境。

words.note: 一个城市就是一个国家：Singapore and Monaco are city-states. 古希腊的雅典也是城邦（city-state）。
words.ctx: More than three decades after it banned the stuff, the city-state shows little sign of relenting.

ex.zh: 新加坡是个小而富裕的城市国家。

words.zh: 令人费解的、莫名其妙的
words.note: baffle（使困惑）+ -ing。I find it baffling that ...（我搞不懂为什么……）
words.ctx: Visitors find the rule baffling; many locals barely notice it.

ex.en: The instructions were completely [[baffling]].
ex.zh: 说明书完全看不懂。

words.note: 挑起眉毛表示惊讶或不赞同：His decision raised a few eyebrows.（他的决定让一些人很惊讶。）
words.ctx: In 1992 Singapore made it illegal to import or sell chewing gum, a law that still raises eyebrows abroad.

ex.en: Her bright green hair [[raised eyebrows]] at the office.
ex.zh: 她那头亮绿色的头发在办公室引人侧目。

ex.en: The price [[raised a few eyebrows]].
ex.zh: 这个价格让一些人吃了一惊。

words.note: the reasoning behind a decision（某个决定背后的理由）。动词 reason（推理）。
words.ctx: The government's reasoning was practical rather than moral.

words.zh: 压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草、忍无可忍
words.note: 来自谚语 the straw that broke the camel's back。That's the last straw!（我受够了！）
words.ctx: The last straw, according to most accounts, came when vandals stuck gum on the door sensors of the new metro trains, causing doors to jam and services to stall.

ex.en: Being late again was [[the last straw]].
ex.zh: 又迟到，这让人忍无可忍了。

ex.en: When the TV broke, that was [[the last straw]].
ex.zh: 电视坏了，这成了压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草。

words.note: fit the description（符合描述），fit the facts（与事实相符）。
words.ctx: But the myth survives because it fits a wider story about a strict little country that likes to keep order.

ex.en: He [[fits]] the description of the thief.
ex.zh: 他符合小偷的特征。

ex.en: Your idea doesn't [[fit]] the facts.
ex.zh: 你的想法和事实对不上。

cloze.before: But the myth survives because it
cloze.after: a wider story about a strict little country that likes to keep order.
cloze.szh: 但这个说法之所以流传下来，是因为它符合一个更大的故事：一个喜欢维持秩序的严格小国。

words.note: for my part（就我而言），for their part（就他们而言）。用来引出某一方的态度。
words.ctx: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.

ex.en: [[For my part]], I'm happy to wait.
ex.zh: 就我而言，我很乐意等。

ex.en: The company, [[for its part]], denies everything.
ex.zh: 公司方面则否认一切。

cloze.before: Singaporeans, for their
cloze.after: , tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.
cloze.szh: 就新加坡人自己而言，他们对这条禁令往往是带着几分好笑的漠不关心。

words.note: 形容词 indifferent（漠不关心的）。with indifference：冷淡地。
words.ctx: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused indifference.

ex.en: He listened with complete [[indifference]].
ex.zh: 他听着，完全无动于衷。

ex.en: She was [[indifferent]] to the news.
ex.zh: 她对这个消息漠不关心。

cloze.before: Singaporeans, for their part, tend to treat the ban with amused
cloze.szh: 就新加坡人自己而言，他们对这条禁令往往是带着几分好笑的漠不关心。

words.note: 也说 get out of the habit of doing。反义 get into the habit（养成习惯）。
words.ctx: Others say they have simply lost the habit.

ex.en: I've [[lost the habit]] of reading before bed.
ex.zh: 我已经不再睡前看书了。

ex.en: Try not to [[get out of the habit]] of exercising.
ex.zh: 尽量别丢了锻炼的习惯。

cloze.before: Others say they have simply lost the
cloze.szh: 也有人说，他们干脆已经没这个习惯了。

words.expr: neither + 助动词 + 主语（倒装）
words.note: 前面是否定句，接“……也不”时用 neither / nor + 助动词 + 主语：I can't swim, and neither can my sister.（我不会游泳，我妹妹也不会。）肯定句用 so：I like tea, and so does she.
words.ctx: Either way, the gum has not come back, and neither has the mess.

ex.en: I haven't seen it, and [[neither has]] Tom.
ex.zh: 我没看过，汤姆也没看过。

ex.en: She loves jazz, and [[so does]] her husband.
ex.zh: 她爱爵士乐，她丈夫也爱。

words.conn: 否定句, and neither + 助动词 + 主语（肯定句用 so + 助动词 + 主语）

pick.q: I don't like horror films, and neither ___ my brother.
pick.why: 前句用 don't（do 的否定），接 neither 时用同一个助动词：neither does。

pick.q: She can speak French, and ___ can her son.
pick.why: 前句是肯定句（can speak），“也会”用 so can her son。

cloze.before: Either way, the gum has not come back, and
cloze.after: has the mess.
cloze.szh: 不管怎样，口香糖没有回来，那些脏乱也没有回来。

words.note: chew on a pencil（咬铅笔）。比喻：Let me chew on it for a day.（让我琢磨一天。）
words.ctx: In Singapore, at least, some problems stay solved because nobody is allowed to chew on them.

ex.en: The dog likes to [[chew on]] my shoes.
ex.zh: 那只狗喜欢啃我的鞋。

ex.en: Give me a day to [[chew on]] your offer.
ex.zh: 给我一天时间琢磨你的提议。

cloze.before: In Singapore, at least, some problems stay solved because nobody is allowed to
cloze.after: on them.
cloze.szh: 至少在新加坡，有些问题一直不再出现，因为谁也不准再“嚼”它们。
